voicequality 390 light.idle:
🔬 Voice QualityBETA ANALYSIS
Hold one comfortable note on an open vowel ("ah") for 4 seconds. Three estimates come from your live microphone signal: vibrato, breathiness and brightness. They are training cues, not a lab or medical measurement.
Hold a note for 4s
Vocal load today
3.6% of daily budget
How it's measured: vibrato is the timing of the peaks in your pitch trace and the swing of each cycle (± cents). Breathiness compares the energy at your harmonics with the noise floor between them, up to 5 kHz, as a harmonics-to-noise ratio (higher = clearer). Brightness is the spectral centroid, the energy-weighted average frequency up to 6 kHz; it's also shown as a multiple of your pitch, because it rises with the note. Noise suppression is off for this measurement so breath noise isn't filtered out.
These are training estimates from your microphone, not a medical assessment. Mic, room, distance, vowel and pitch all move them, so compare yourself on the same setup, note and vowel. The bands (for example, 20 dB or more reads as clear) are rough guides for this tool, not clinical norms. If hoarseness or breathiness persists, or singing hurts, a voice teacher or voice professional is the right person to ask.
